candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — legal/regulatory responsibilities and staffing/resource management
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — jurisdiction-specific nurse staffing regulation
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that nurse-staffing law and regulation vary by jurisdiction and require current local verification.

options.A: Jurisdictions may use different approaches, including staffing committees, disclosure requirements, or legislated staffing ratios/standards, so current local law must be checked
options.B: No state uses staffing-related laws, regulations, reporting requirements, or ratio standards
options.C: Every state uses the same mandatory nurse-to-patient ratios for comparable hospital units
options.D: Only federal law can regulate hospital nurse staffing, so states have no role

candidate.rationale: ANA's current state-policy materials show that nurse-staffing policy is not uniform across jurisdictions. Approaches include nurse-led staffing committees, mandated staffing disclosure, and legislated minimum ratios or standards. Because requirements change, nurses and leaders should verify current jurisdiction-specific law and regulation rather than assume a national uniform rule. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: U.S. nurse-staffing policy varies by jurisdiction and may use different regulatory approaches rather than one uniform nationwide state model.
candidate.source_document_title: ANA Membership Assembly Convenes in the Year of the Power of Nurses; State Government Affairs Program
